ledger.note: 1180: the Prince-Bishopric of Münster appears on the collapse of Saxony ('Created on collapse of Saxony: 1180'); the bishop had the city's administration from 1173 and imperial princely rank from 1220.
1252: the see buys Vechta and Meppen. 'In 1252 Countess Jutta von Vechta-Ravensberg sold Meppen to the Bishop of Münster'; the see bought the County of Vechta.

region.text: the County of Vechta and Meppen on the Ems

ledger.note: 1403: the Cloppenburg and Oyte district. 'The district around Cloppenburg and Oyte was gained' in 1403; the page names no seller (the Oldenburg counts are the researcher's reading).

region.text: the district round Cloppenburg and Oyte

ledger.note: 1406: Ahaus and Stromberg. The Ahaus manorial domain and Stromberg castle 'with its jurisdiction' were acquired.

region.text: the lordship of Ahaus and Stromberg castle

ledger.note: 1429: Wildeshausen is pledged to Münster. 'Wildeshausen was taken in pledge from the Prince-Archbishopric of Bremen'; the pledge is renewed in 1679 (Treaty of Nijmegen) with a 100,000 riksdaler loan to Sweden.
February 1534: the Anabaptists take Münster. 'The city was under Anabaptist rule from February 1534, when the city hall was seized'; Franz von Waldeck, the expelled bishop, besieged it.
24 June 1535: the city falls. 'After lengthy resistance, the city was taken by the besiegers on June 24, 1535.' John of Leiden and others were captured and executed in January 1536.

1802: Prussia takes the bishopric. Infobox 'Secularised to Prussia: 1802'; a secret Franco-Prussian agreement of 5 August 1796 had chosen the prince-bishopric as Prussian compensation for lost left-bank Rhine lands; Prussia took formal possession in March 1803.

1803: Oldenburg receives the north: 'The Duchy of Oldenburg received much of the Prince-Bishopric of Münster' (mediatisation page); the Münster page: 'Oldenburg gained the northern part (Vechta and Cloppenburg)'.

1803: Arenberg, Looz-Corswarem, Salm and Croÿ 'received other parts as compensation'. The page assigns no town; the Ems district (Meppen) and the Ahaus domain are the remainder after Prussia and Oldenburg.

region.text: the remaining parts: the Ems district and Ahaus

ledger.note: 1803: 'In 1803 the bishopric, with c. 310,000 inhabitants was secularized by the Reichsdeputationshauptschluss.'
March 1803: Prussia takes possession of its eastern share under the Reichsdeputationshauptschluss.
1803: Prussia receives the eastern share: 'Prussia took the larger eastern share, which it took possession of in March 1803'; 'In 1815 Prussia was given the southern part (Oberstift).'

region.text: the larger eastern share, round Münster

wars.name: Münster Rebellion
wars.outcome: The prince-bishop's army takes the Anabaptist city on 24 June 1535; the leaders are executed in January 1536.

wars.name: Münster-Dutch war and the Treaty of Cleves
wars.outcome: Galen was 'compelled ... to make a disadvantageous peace in 1666 in Cleve'; no border moved on the pages opened.
wars.note: The page gives neither the start of the war nor the treaty date.

wars.name: Franco-Dutch War (Münster's part)
wars.outcome: Galen allied with Louis XIV and took Groenlo, Deventer and Coevorden; 'In October 1674 he withdrew his troops from the Dutch Republic', and in 1675 turned against France.
wars.note: The 1672 start rests on a link title on the page. No Münster land changed hands; the conquests were Dutch land (the Dutch dossier's events).

wars.name: Galen's war with Sweden over Bremen-Verden
wars.outcome: Galen 'attacked Charles XI of Sweden, and conquered the Duchy of Bremen'; the page gives no dates and no lasting gain.
wars.note: The Münster page says he 'gained parts of the Prince-Archbishopric of Bremen and of the Prince-Bishopric of Verden' in 1650-1678.

certainty.note: The pages give towns and districts, not boundaries; the Oberstift and the Niederstift (Vechta, Meppen, Cloppenburg) were joined only by a strip.

notes:
Written 2026-10-25 for batch eu-09-x (4 pages opened; budget 5). New state: Cliopatria has no Münster row.

SHAPES ARE RADIUS READINGS: Münster 45 km, Meppen (7.29E 52.69N) 35 km, Vechta (8.29E 52.73N) 25 km, Cloppenburg (8.05E 52.85N) 20 km, Ahaus (7.01E 52.08N) 15 km, Wildeshausen (8.43E 52.90N) 15 km. Gazetteer names wanted: 'Meppen', 'Vechta', 'Cloppenburg', 'Ahaus', 'Wildeshausen'.

NOT SETTLED. (1) The infobox says 'Secularised to Prussia: 1802' and the text 1803; the dossier ends in February 1803 (Final Recess) and records a 1802 Prussian occupation. (2) The Galen conquests of Bremen-Verden (page: 'gained parts' in 1650-1678) are undated and not drawn; the 1679 pledge renewal for Wildeshausen is a loan to Sweden, not a gain. (3) The 1661 occupation of the city of Münster by Galen is internal and not an event. (4) The sellers in 1403 and 1406 are not named by the page. (5) The 1569 transfer of western Frisian territory to the bishoprics of Groningen and Deventer is ecclesiastical, not drawn. (6) The personal unions with Paderborn, Osnabrück and Cologne are only general periods on the page. (7) No ruler list was opened.
